name: golden byte-identical ROM invariants
why: The crown-jewel guard. "Unused features are stripped, so ROMs stay byte-identical" is the single property that makes every engine change cheap to verify, and CLAUDE.md names it as the standing guardrail — but neither golden assertion had ever been watched failing.
anchor_note: BOTH breaks were verified BY HAND to move the ROM hash before being written here (jmp_up 20->21 gives b7aea34f vs golden 1730448e, for the stock build and the template build alike). That verification is not ceremony — two earlier anchors were wrong and each produced a 'nothing caught this' result that looked exactly like a hollow guard. (1) #define DEADZONE_LEFT is DEAD: scroll.c takes its own default from scroll.h, and main.c never uses its own copy, so the build was byte-identical. (2) The `{ jumping = 1; jmp_up = 20; }` form on platformer.c:1389 sits inside `#if BW_GAME_STYLE == 2 && PLAYER2_ENABLED` and is stripped from a no-modules build — pointedly, that is the very property this invariant exists to guarantee. A break that does not change the output proves nothing about the guard, and 'stayed green' cannot tell you which of the two you have. Measure the hash first.

expect: invariant - Step_Playground stock ROM matches golden hash

breaks.find:
//>> jump_height: How high the player jumps. Bigger number = higher jump (try 10 to 40).
                jmp_up = 20;
breaks.replace:
//>> jump_height: How high the player jumps. Bigger number = higher jump (try 10 to 40).
                jmp_up = 21;
expect: invariant - template (no modules) ROM matches golden hash
